title: decision-verdict/1: what a decision verifier concluded about one act, and why (DEC-0172)
description: A receipt, never an authority (DV-1): a callee never takes a verdict as a decision, and an allow names the route by which a form the callee already accepts reaches it. Its id derives from {askedDigest, caller, policy, session} (verdictId); the arguments themselves, the operator's instruction and source never ride in it. A checker reports a verdict whose parts do not agree, and an allow the reference refuses, as FAC-SEM-179. docs/specification/decision-verdict.md.

id.description: sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of {askedDigest, caller, policy, session} (verdictId): the same act asked again in one session under one policy has one id; the verifier's journal keeps each answer to it as a new version.

expiresAt.description: allow: at most the earliest of its grounds' windows and never more than 15 minutes after at; human: at most 24 hours; deny: at most 1 hour, person-denied at most 24 hours (FAC-SEM-179).

capability.description: The tool the call names; the hub matches it with the call's capability (DV-8).

action.description: The call's decision.action where it carries a decision (the action's id in the callee's actions extension), else its capability (a call under a mandate, the callee's own elicitation, the caller's own act): the hub matches it the same way (DV-8).

effect.description: The DL-3 effect class: the callee's declared actionEffects where it declares one, else the capability's effect as a floor (DV-5).

target.description: The one object the act acts on, as the callee identifies it; one that names a person is carried as hmac-sha256: under the host's own key, never a plain hash a reader could reverse by guessing.

argsDigest.description: HMAC-SHA-256 under the host's own key of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the call's input (argsDigest): never the arguments themselves, and no plain hash a reader could reverse by guessing.

actionDigest.description: The action's digest (DL-18), where the callee declares the object it is computed over (actionObject, DV-5) or its refusal gave it.

spendUsd.description: The act's worst-case cost: the callee's declared maxCostUsd where it declares one, else the call's own estimate; DV-7 compares it with the limits.

asked.description: The deciding values and digests of the act, never its arguments.

askedDigest.description: sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of asked.

caller.description: The principal the host authenticated; in an organization's context the host's pairwise id for that organization, as LV-9's approver is, never a person's address.

session.description: The session the host authenticated; in an organization's context a pairwise id, as caller.

rule.description: The contract rule that decided, by its id (spend-rule-3 for the spend policy's rule 3), a policy row (row:<id>), or the person's answer (answer:<questionId>) for person-denied and rejected.

reason.description: allow: covered; human: body-gate, kept, level-insufficient, not-covered, outside-window, evidence-unknown, evidence-stale, ground-invalid, vetoed, loop, voided, spend-limit, row-advised; deny: forbidden, other-context, self-approval, person-denied, rejected (FAC-SEM-179 keeps each in its verdict's group).

route.description: With allow only: how the reference takes the act (FAC-SEM-179).

machineForm.description: With allow only: how the form reaches the callee, never the form itself: caller-approval with route approval, executed-by-holder with route level, none exactly with own-act, hub-dispatch otherwise (FAC-SEM-179).

grounds.description: Each a form or a requirement the verifier read, by id or digest. An authority's grade says what the reference takes from this caller at its tier (verified, taken, forwarded) or not (data); a grant, a budget or a check carries no grade and never grounds an allow (a budget is read, not reserved). An entitlement (DEC-0168) is no ground.

policy.description: The verifier's policy table it read, by version and digest.

addressees.description: Principals by their host id, never a person's address; empty for advice that asks no one.

human.description: With human only: who is asked (none for advice), the question, or an AP-4 step with its link once the callee's refusal gave it.
